math_errors.error: Per-step error is stated as ≈ Δs·Δθ² ≈ 4.5e-6 m/step and then claimed to stay 'mm 이하' after 1 h. The exact per-step midpoint error is Δs·cosφ·[1 − sinc(Δθ/2)] ≈ Δs·Δθ²/24 = 1.9e-7 m (the 1/24 factor is dropped), and 1 h at 100 Hz is 3.6e5 steps: 3.6e5 × 4.5e-6 = 1.6 m by the brief's own number, 0.07 m with the exact value — neither is 'mm 이하'.
math_errors.correction: State the error as a relative scale error Δθ²/24 (≤ 9.4e-6 at 1.5 rad/s, 100 Hz), i.e. ≤ 7 cm over 7.2 km worst case, negligible against the 0.5 % radius-ratio error; remove the 'mm 이하' sentence and make the unit test compare against the arc solution with this bound.

math_errors.location: §2.2 line 58/62 and §2.3 line 78 (δ²/6 quantisation term inside Σ_u for pose propagation)
math_errors.error: The brief itself notes that the per-step quantisation error of Δn is MA(1) with negative correlation (it telescopes; cumulative count error is bounded by ±δ/2 per wheel), yet δ²/6 is added to Σ_u and propagated as white process noise in Σ^p_{k+1} = F_p Σ F_pᵀ + F_u Σ_u F_uᵀ. This manufactures a spurious random walk: n·δ²/6 per wheel ≈ 7.9e-4 m² (σ ≈ 2.8 cm) after 1 h, and Var(θ) grows by n·δ²/(3b²) although the true heading quantisation error is bounded by ≈ δ/b ≈ 3e-4 rad.
math_errors.correction: Keep δ²/6 (or δ²/12 per velocity) only in the twist (velocity) covariance where the difference is genuinely taken; in the pose propagation either omit it or add a single bounded term (δ²/12 per wheel) once, not per step.

math_errors.location: §2.3 line 80 ('+ F_ρ Σ_ρ F_ρᵀ') and §4.3 line 187 (hᵀΣ_ψh, (b/2)²[φ̇]Σ_ψ[φ̇]ᵀ added to twist covariance)
math_errors.error: A constant parameter error (r_L, r_R, b) is perfectly correlated across steps, but adding F_ρ Σ_ρ F_ρᵀ every step models it as white per-step noise, giving Var ∝ L instead of the correct Var(θ) ∝ L² and Var(y) ∝ L⁴ for systematic errors (the brief's own §2.2 numbers: 0.29 rad and 2.9 m after 20 m are deterministic, not √L). robot_localization likewise whitens the hᵀΣ_ψh term in the twist covariance, so the EKF remains over-confident over long straight runs.
math_errors.correction: Either augment the odometry state with ρ (or ψ) and propagate the cross-covariance Σ_{pρ} (F_p Σ_{pρ} + F_ρ Σ_ρ), or state explicitly that the per-step term is a lower bound and that the systematic component is handled by GRC convergence, not by covariance.

math_errors.error: (a) For the quantisation part, a_enc = (n(t) − 2n(t−T_w) + n(t−2T_w))/T_w² is a second difference sharing the middle count, so Var_q(a) = 6σ_q²/T_w⁴, not 4σ_q²/T_w⁴ (1.5× understated). (b) Far worse: the 7e-3 m/s² figure counts quantisation only and ignores the brief's own slip term k|Δs_i|. With k = 1e-5 m (the value used in §2.4), T_w = 0.1 s, v = 1–2 m/s: Var(Δs_i) = k·vT_w ⇒ σ_v ≈ 0.007–0.010 m/s ⇒ σ_a = √2·σ_v/T_w ≈ 0.10–0.14 m/s², 15–20× larger than stated. A 0.3 m/s² slip residual then contributes r_a²/S_a ≈ 4.6–9 < τ_on = 9.21, so the accelerometer channel cannot reliably detect the very slip it is meant to catch, and the '여유 충분' conclusion is false.
math_errors.correction: Recompute S_a with σ_i² = k_i|Δs_i| + δ²/6 and the 6σ_q² double-difference factor; either lengthen T_w for the acceleration channel (S_a ∝ 1/T_w for the slip term), use an integrated velocity residual Δv_enc − ∫a_imu over the window (variance ∝ T_w, not 1/T_w²), or drop the claim that the channel resolves 0.3 m/s² events.

math_errors.location: §4.2 line 165 (a_enc from window differencing) vs. §3.3 line 145 (accelerometer LPF group delay 16 ms)
math_errors.error: a_enc computed from v_enc(t) − v_enc(t−T_w), with each v_enc a window mean, is centred at t − T_w (≈100 ms lag), whereas the LPF'd a_imu is centred at t − 16 ms. The residual r_a therefore contains jerk × 84 ms during every normal acceleration ramp (reaching the spec's 1 m/s² within ~0.1 s ⇒ ~10 m/s³ ⇒ up to ~0.8 m/s² spurious residual), guaranteeing false alarms at each start/stop even without slip.
math_errors.correction: Align both signals to the same time centre (average a_imu over the same [t−2T_w, t] window or delay it by T_w − τ_c), and add an acceleration-ramp (no-slip) dataset to the false-alarm unit test.

math_errors.error: With Δt = 10 ms and α = Δt/(τ_c+Δt) (backward-Euler), the discrete −3 dB frequencies are 13.7 Hz (not 20 Hz) and 7.9 Hz (not 10 Hz) because f_c/f_s = 0.1–0.2 is far from the small-ratio regime; the '군지연 ≈ τ_c' statement is likewise only asymptotic.
math_errors.correction: Use a bilinear design with prewarping (or α = 1 − e^{−2πf_cΔt} and report the resulting −3 dB point), and set the 'LPF −3 dB' unit-test target to the exact discrete value.

math_errors.location: §3.3 line 148 (Allan variance from a '30 분 정지 로그' with τ = 300 s Gauss–Markov bias)
math_errors.error: At cluster time τ = 300 s a 30-min record yields M = 6 clusters, so σ_A(300 s) has ≈ ±30 % (1σ) uncertainty and the bias-instability floor / correlation time cannot be identified; the curve would only be trustworthy up to τ ≈ 20–30 s.
math_errors.correction: Log ≥ 3–5 h of static IMU data (cheap in simulation, can be run faster than real time) or restrict the claimed identification to N (ARW) and quote the confidence interval σ_A·(2(M−1))^{-1/2}.

math_errors.location: §4.3 line 183 ('λ ∈ [0.995, 0.9995]') with the 100 Hz update rate
math_errors.error: λ = 0.995 at 100 Hz is a 200-sample (2 s) memory, λ = 0.9995 is 20 s. In a direction that is not excited (ψ_R+ψ_L during long straight corridors) plain exponential forgetting makes P grow as λ^{−k}: ×1.2e13 after 60 s at λ = 0.995 (×20 at 0.9995), so the first rotation after a corridor produces an arbitrarily large jump in ψ̂ and a numerically unusable P. 'cond(P) 감시로 동결' is mentioned but is not part of the stated update equations.
math_errors.correction: Make directional forgetting / constant-trace regulation (Gu et al. 2026, which the brief already cites) or a bounded-trace reset part of the baseline update, and choose λ so that the memory (1/(1−λ)) is ≥ several minutes at 100 Hz (λ ≥ 0.9999) or update at the window rate rather than per sample.

math_errors.location: §4.2 line 168 ('오경보 ≤ 1 %') and §6 unit test 'χ² 검출 오경보 ≤ 1 %'
math_errors.error: τ_on = 9.21 is the p = 0.01 quantile per test; at 10–20 tests/s with a mandatory 0.2 s hold, the fraction of time flagged under H0 is ≥ 2–4 % by construction, so the ≤ 1 % target is inconsistent with the chosen threshold. The χ²₂ assumption also requires Gaussian white residuals, while the quantisation error is uniform/MA(1) and the LPF'd accelerometer noise is coloured.
math_errors.correction: Define the FA metric (per-test vs. time-fraction), pick τ_on accordingly (e.g. p = 0.001 or require k-of-n exceedances as De Giorgi 2023 does), and validate the null distribution empirically on no-slip runs.

math_errors.location: §2.2 line 65 (WheelSlip: '적재 25 kg 시 F_N 변화 → 유효 슬립 변화')
math_errors.error: In gz-sim6 WheelSlip.cc (verified) `wheel_normal_force` is a fixed SDF parameter, not a measured contact force: slip1/2 = compliance·r|ω|/F_N,param and are applied as ODE force-dependent-slip coefficients, so slip velocity = slip1/2 × actual friction force. Adding payload increases the true contact force and therefore *increases* simulated slip velocity unless F_N,param is updated — opposite to the physical intuition the sentence implies.
math_errors.correction: State explicitly how payload-dependent slip will be emulated (update `wheel_normal_force` per payload, or use the runtime `WheelSlipCmd` component the plugin exposes, which also gives a cheap way to emulate low-friction patches without world geometry).

math_errors.location: §4.2 line 176 ('슬립 중 Δθ 를 (ω_g − b̂_g)Δt 로 대체') vs. §4.4 line 203 ('twist=(v,0,ω_enc)')
math_errors.error: During slip the pose in /wheel_odom is integrated with the gyro rate while the published twist still carries ω_enc, so pose ≠ ∫twist inside the same message. Since the EKF fuses twist only (odom0_config vx, vy, vyaw) and already fuses the IMU vyaw, the gyro substitution changes nothing in the EKF output that the spec targets are measured on.
math_errors.correction: Either publish ω = ω_g during slip with the IMU term excluded from the EKF (double-counting must be avoided) or, preferably, keep the substitution for the standalone odometry pose only and re-scope the expected gain (§4.6) to the raw-odometry heading error, not to the EKF/AMCL error.

proposal_verdicts.proposal: SACO — Slip-Adaptive Covariance Odometry (χ² gated 2-channel slip detector + covariance inflation + gyro-substituted heading)
proposal_verdicts.reasoning: Implementable in weeks and cheap, but (i) every block has closer published prior art than the brief admits: the accelerometer longitudinal-consistency test c21(ω_R,k−ω_R,k−1)+c22(ω_L,k−ω_L,k−1)−a_x Δt with a datasheet threshold checked over several steps is eq. (8)/(10) of De Giorgi et al. 2023 — a paper the brief cites — not Oeltjen 2025/Yu 2023 as §4.5 states; χ²-gated slip-event classification on residuals is in Kuncara et al. 2024 (Measurement); inflating the wheel-odometry measurement covariance on an encoder-vs-IMU yaw-rate residual is publicly implemented (rouf-rimon/adaptive-ekf-slip-detector, R_odom = R_nom(1+500λ)) and learned/online odometry covariances are in Brossard & Bonnabel ICRA 2019 and Okawara 2024. What remains new is only the quantisation-aware normalisation and the robot_localization twist-covariance packaging. (ii) The accelerometer channel as specified does not work at the brief's own noise model: S_a is understated ~20× (σ_a ≈ 0.10–0.14 m/s² at 1–2 m/s, not 7e-3), and the 84 ms misalignment between a_enc and LPF'd a_imu creates false alarms on every acceleration ramp. (iii) The headline gain ('>50 % heading-error reduction') concerns the standalone odometry pose, which the EKF does not consume; the EKF already has the gyro, so the spec-relevant benefit is limited to consistency (NEES) and is unquantified. (iv) FA ≤ 1 % contradicts τ_on at p = 0.01 with a 0.2 s hold.
proposal_verdicts.evidence: De Giorgi, De Palma, Parlangeli, Robotics 13(1):7, 2023 (full text fetched: §3.1 eqs. 7–10, slippage detected from IMU acceleration consistency incl. frontal-acceleration residual; batch LS calibration). Kuncara et al., Measurement 2024, DOI 10.1016/j.measurement.2024.114903 (χ² slip-event test, 3 DOF, threshold 4.642 — search-snippet level). github.com/rouf-rimon/adaptive-ekf-slip-detector (encoder–IMU yaw-rate residual, covariance inflation). Brossard & Bonnabel, ICRA 2019, DOI 10.1109/icra.2019.8794237. Reina, Ojeda, Milella, Borenstein, IEEE/ASME T-Mech 2006, DOI 10.1109/tmech.2006.871095 (encoder/gyro discrepancy slip detection). Numerical check: k = 1e-5 m, T_w = 0.1 s, v = 2 m/s ⇒ σ_v = 0.010 m/s, σ_a = 0.14 m/s²; χ²₂ 0.99 quantile = 9.21.

proposal_verdicts.proposal: GRC — Gyro-Referenced Recursive Least-Squares wheel-parameter calibration with covariance feedback
proposal_verdicts.reasoning: The linear-in-parameters gyro model z = φ̇_R ψ_R − φ̇_L ψ_L is correct, the observability split (straight ⇒ ψ_R−ψ_L, rotation ⇒ ψ_R+ψ_L) is right, scale unobservability is honestly stated, the recovery b̂ = 2r̄/(ψ̂_R+ψ̂_L) is consistent, and 5 % → 1 % convergence within ~60 s of mixed driving is realistic in simulation. It is correctly labelled a variant, but the positioning must be fixed: ψ = [r_R/b, r_L/b] is exactly Antonelli et al.'s c21/c22 (T-RO 2005; Autonomous Robots 2007 'Linear estimation of the physical odometric parameters'), the straight/rotation observability decomposition with heading-error references is Jung & Chung (ICRA 2012 / IJARS 2011), and online augmented-KF estimation of (r_L, r_R, b) with heading references and covariance feedback exists (Martinelli et al., Auton. Robots 2006; Cantelli et al., Robotics 2016). De Giorgi 2023 is *not* gyro-referenced or recursive (batch LS over P trajectories with known end poses, assumption A4), so calling GRC 'De Giorgi 의 변형' is inaccurate — it is closer to Antonelli 2007 + Jung–Chung 2012 with an RLS. Required fixes before it is credible: directional forgetting / bounded trace as part of the update (λ = 0.995 at 100 Hz is a 2 s memory and P explodes ×1e13 in 60 s unexcited); decoupling from SACO (the RLS drives r_ω to zero, so a slow persistent asymmetric slip that stays under τ_on is absorbed into ψ̂ — add rate limits/physical bounds on ψ and innovation monitoring); and the per-step whitening of hᵀΣ_ψh in the EKF covariance (see math_errors).
proposal_verdicts.evidence: Antonelli, Chiaverini, Fusco, IEEE T-RO 21, 2005, DOI 10.1109/TRO.2005.851382 (Crossref verified); Antonelli & Chiaverini, Autonomous Robots 2007, DOI 10.1007/s10514-007-9030-2 (Crossref verified); Jung & Chung, ICRA 2012, DOI 10.1109/icra.2012.6224660 and IJARS 2011, DOI 10.5772/50906 (Crossref verified); Martinelli, Tomatis, Siegwart, Autonomous Robots 2006, DOI 10.1007/s10514-006-9006-7; Cantelli et al., Robotics 5(4):23, 2016, DOI 10.3390/robotics5040023 (EKF estimating wheel radii, wheelbase and magnetometer offset online); De Giorgi et al. 2023 full text §3 (eqs. 14–23: batch LS, assumption A4 known initial/final poses). Numerical check: λ^{-6000} = 1.2e13 for λ = 0.995.

spec_gaps: TF frame convention: the spec's TF tree (line ~417) is map → odom → base_footprint → base_link, but the brief publishes /wheel_odom with child_frame_id = base_link and states 'odom→base_link 는 EKF 만 발행' (§2.5 line 108, §6 line 248). robot_localization must then use base_link_frame = base_footprint (Nav2 convention) or the tree must drop base_footprint; as written the EKF would publish odom→base_link while the URDF publishes base_footprint→base_link, producing a TF conflict. The brief must fix the frame names and state which node publishes odom→base_footprint.

Spec 3 (위치 추정) requires RMSE *and* Maximum Error against ground truth for every accuracy claim, in the [timestamp, gt_x, gt_y, est_x, est_y, error] format with ≥ 100 samples; §5 T1/T2 report only '최종 오차 / 오차/L' and only T4 mentions max error. Make RMSE + max error (and the log) mandatory outputs of T1, T2, T3, T6 and specify that the 3/5/8 cm targets are evaluated on the fused EKF output (T6 '정지' is currently an odometry/IMU-only test).

IMU gravity handling is unspecified: §3.3 removes bias only ('가속도는 중력 제거' applies to the bias estimate), so /imu/data linear_acceleration still contains gravity per sensor_msgs/Imu convention, while the spec's EKF example fuses ax, ay. The brief must state imu0_remove_gravitational_acceleration: true (or remove gravity in the node) and how roll/pitch (needed for that removal) are obtained when orientation_covariance[0] = −1.

Spec 10 requires a 4-hour continuous-operation test; the brief only notes int64 tick counters. No plan for 4 h stability of GRC (ψ̂ drift with forgetting), SACO decay states, covariance boundedness of /wheel_odom pose, or topic-rate/latency over 4 h. Add a T9 endurance run (can be sim-time accelerated).

Spec sensor section requires documented sensor-calibration procedures and an extrinsic parameter file; the brief covers only intrinsic (r_L, r_R, b) calibration. State explicitly that extrinsics (lidar_link, camera_link, imu_link offsets and the IMU lever-arm l_x used in §3.3) are owned by another area or add them.

Spec 10 requires ≥ 10 automated integration scenarios; §6 mentions launch_pytest integration tests without enumerating scenarios. List the integration scenarios contributed by this area (e.g. tick-emulator ↔ bridge, filtered scan into costmap, IMU node into EKF).

The spec's EKF example fuses IMU yaw (imu0_config yaw = true); the brief's recommendation to publish orientation_covariance[0] = −1 is justified (gz-sensors6 ImuSensor.cc applies noise only to angular velocity and linear acceleration — verified) but it is a deviation from the spec example that needs an explicit decision record, including the fallback (publish a noisy integrated yaw) if the localisation team keeps yaw = true.

Depth pipeline: the spec requires 640×480 with '깊이 측정 노이즈' applied; §3.2 sets a constant σ = 0.01 m in Gazebo and mentions a Z-dependent model only as commentary. State which noise model is applied in the SDF and how the height-crop and voxel thresholds were derived from it (a 1 cm σ at 5 m yields ~3 cm spread; the 0.05 m crop floor is then marginal).
required_revisions: §2.1 line 49: replace the 'mm 이하' sentence with the relative scale-error statement Δθ²/24 and the correct per-step value 1.9e-7 m; keep the arc-vs-midpoint unit test against this bound.

§2.2/§2.3: remove δ²/6 from the pose-propagation Σ_u (or add it once, bounded) and keep it only in the twist covariance; document the MA(1) structure and its effect on windowed differences (6σ_q² for second differences).

§2.3 line 80 / §4.3 line 187: either augment the state with ψ and propagate Σ_{pψ}, or state that F_ρΣ_ρF_ρᵀ / hᵀΣ_ψh are per-step lower bounds and that systematic error is removed by calibration, not covered by covariance; add a note that robot_localization whitens these terms.

§4.2: recompute S_a with the full noise model (k|Δs| + δ²/6, 6σ_q² factor), time-align a_enc and a_imu, redefine the FA metric and threshold consistently, and add an acceleration-ramp no-slip dataset to the detector unit test; if the channel still cannot resolve 0.3 m/s² at 2 m/s, replace it with an integrated velocity residual or drop the 'symmetric slip' claim.

§4.2/§4.4: make the message self-consistent (pose = ∫ published twist) and re-scope the expected gain of gyro substitution to the standalone odometry pose; state that the spec-relevant benefit is EKF consistency (NEES/NIS) and quantify it as the primary SACO metric.

§4.3: put directional forgetting / constant-trace (Gu et al. 2026) or bounded-trace reset into the RLS equations, raise λ (or update at window rate), add physical bounds and a rate limit on ψ̂, and add innovation monitoring so slow slips are not absorbed; specify the interaction order between SACO gating and RLS.

§4.5 novelty table: re-attribute the accelerometer residual channel to De Giorgi et al. 2023 eqs. (7)–(10); describe De Giorgi correctly (batch LS over P trajectories with known end poses, IMU motion reconstruction during slip) and re-position GRC against Antonelli 2005/2007 (c21/c22 parameterisation), Jung & Chung 2011/2012 (straight/rotation heading-error observability), Martinelli 2006 and Cantelli 2016 (online augmented-KF estimation of r_L, r_R, b with covariance); add Kuncara et al. 2024 (χ² slip gating) and Brossard & Bonnabel 2019 / public adaptive-EKF implementations as prior art for covariance inflation.
§2.2 line 65: correct the WheelSlip description (fixed `wheel_normal_force`, ODE force-dependent slip, WheelSlipCmd runtime updates) and specify the payload-slip emulation protocol used in T4.

§3.3: fix the LPF −3 dB numbers (13.7 Hz / 7.9 Hz with the current α, or use a prewarped bilinear design), lengthen the Allan-variance log to ≥ 3–5 h or quote confidence intervals, and specify gravity handling for the published linear_acceleration.
§3.2 line 138: remove or properly cite the dangling '2025 flock 논문' reference.

§2.5 line 106 / ref 33: the 'do not fuse derivative-related fields' rule is not in the robot_localization preparing_sensor_data doc (verified) and the Nav2 odometry page could not be fetched (404); either cite the exact source text or delete the claim; keep the verified facts (0 → 1e-6 epsilon, no covariance inflation to ignore variables, twist transformed from child_frame_id to base_link_frame, ENU).
